terminalFinding.cause: The watchdog correctly rejected the command before process creation; R45 spent the invocation budget generating the post-receipt union, counts, research packet and 138-KB config.

importPathFinding.finding: The zc import-path problem is a separate latent launch-environment defect; R45 never started far enough to encounter it.
whyAuthorizedIntegrationMissedIt: The integration test generated a custom wrapper that explicitly inserted the dictionary root into sys.path.
It also invoked the watchdog with cwd equal to the dictionary root.
Those two test-only conditions guarantee that top-level zc.py and atomic_write.py are importable.

A direct absolute-path execution of a script under maintenance from another working directory begins with maintenance, not the dictionary root, on sys.path and can therefore fail to import top-level zc.
The test proved compilation under its injected environment, but did not prove that production and test shared one canonical invocation environment.

behavior: Restricts the target script to the active dictionary root.
Pins cwd to the active dictionary root.
Prepends that root to PYTHONPATH while preserving any existing value.
Uses the current Python interpreter and returns the child exit code.
processRepair.futureInvocationRule: Both integration tests and production watchdog commands must bind and invoke this exact wrapper; cohort-specific sys.path wrappers are prohibited.

coverage: From /tmp with PYTHONPATH removed, a script inside the dictionary root imports the real zc.py and atomic_write.py and observes cwd equal to the dictionary root.
A target script outside the dictionary root is rejected.
